input:
Earlier scenes:
古代的时候人觉得祭拜非常重要，孟子很小的时候，从早到晚一直祭拜，因为他妈妈告诉他祭拜很重要。虽然他没有朋友，因为每天只祭拜。他的同学们老是对他开玩笑了。孟子妈妈看了他的同学们对孟子不好的影响，所以孟子和孟子妈妈搬家了。孟子才十一岁，成为一个哲学家。孟子不是祭拜，而是看政治文章，难怪他成为了哲学家。不过，看过很多政治文章对他害得，他有很多问题。

This scene:
他一直问问题，但是不能解决那些问题。孟子长大，他开始能解决问题。他常常建议你不是学金融，而是学政治，因为如果你懂政治，你会成为高薪。后来孟子成为教授，他教学生很厉害。

The teacher's corrections on this scene (student words：her correction, her note):
- 孟子长大，他开始能解决问题：长大以后，delete他，redundant
- 他常常建议你不是学金融，而是学政治：建议人们，不要学金融
- 因为如果你懂政治，你会成为高薪：delete the second你，redundant; 得到高薪，成为 + profession/celebrity

The system's feedback items:
1. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 成为高薪：成为高薪人士，"高薪" means a high salary, so a person cannot become it; "高薪人士" means a person with a high salary.
2. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 建议你不是学金融，而是学政治：建议你不要学金融，而要学政治，after "建议", use "不要……而要……" to recommend one action instead of another; "不是……而是……" states a factual contrast.
3. [Coherence: reference, error] Coherence (Reference): 孟子长大：他长大了，use a pronoun for a close re-occurrence when the same character was named in the immediately preceding sentence and no other character competes as the referent.
4. [Coherence: reference, error] Coherence (Reference): 你：学生，this second-person pronoun has no introduced addressee and abruptly addresses the reader; use a full noun phrase to identify who receives his advice.
5. [Coherence: temporality, error] Coherence (Temporality): 孟子长大：他长大了，use "了" after "长大" to mark the completed change of state.
6. [Coherence: temporality, error] Coherence (Temporality): 后来孟子成为教授：后来孟子成为了教授，use "了" to mark the completed change of becoming a professor.

items.reason: “高薪” is a salary, so a person cannot become it; “高薪人士” is a valid noun for a person.
For advice about what not to study and what to study instead, “不要……而要……” is appropriate here.
孟子 has already been established as the only current character, so the close re-reference should be “他” rather than repeating his name.
“你” has no introduced addressee, whereas “学生” clearly identifies the people receiving his advice.
Growing up is a completed change of state in this past narrative, so “长大了” is appropriate.
Becoming a professor is a completed narrative event, so “成为了教授” correctly marks completion.
